items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a noun-plus-する (suru) verb in the dictionary form this lesson introduces.

items.note: The lesson's core frame: person は — thing が — すきです. にほんの here means "of Japan", i.e. Japanese.

items.note: The pair to たなかさんはにほんごをはなします: を stays with はなす, and の wraps the whole action so が can mark it as the thing liked.

items.target: にほんごをはなすのがすきです

items.note: みるの turns the verb into the thing liked — the nominalizer only ever follows a dictionary form. Contrast にほんのアニメ, where の joins two nouns instead.

items.note: え is what かく takes as its object (を), and the whole action えをかく is what の turns into the thing liked (が). Two different particles, two different jobs.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: EXERCISES VII substitution 2; job: を inside a のが clause, the pattern's hardest shape).
items.target: グリーンさんはえをかくのがすきですか

items.note: This の joins two nouns: いとこ の ポール, "Paul, [who is] my cousin." It is the same の as にほんのアニメ, and NOT the nominalizer の of かくのがすきです — that one only ever follows a verb.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: Target Dialogue; job: possessive/appositive の, and the contrast with this lesson's nominalizer の).

items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a dictionary-form verb on Lesson 7's じてんしゃ (jitensha), and the に (ni) it takes is the part a learner gets wrong.

items.target: すいえいをします
items.note: すいえい (suiei) is a NOUN meaning swimming as a sport or discipline, so it needs します to become something you do: まいしゅう すいえいを します (maishū suiei o shimasu), 'I swim every week'. しゅみは すいえい です (shumi wa suiei desu) = 'my hobby is swimming'. For the physical act, use およぐ (oyogu).
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 15 teaches suiei and the sport/hobby set

items.note: Contrast with サッカーをみるのがすきです: this one likes the SPORT, that one likes WATCHING it. A plain noun takes が on its own; an action needs のが to become one.
